exercise.name: Lever Seated Hip Abduction

reference.title: Lever Seated Hip Abduction
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page was not opened from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read and the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Hip abduction machine (selectorized, two lever arms on vertical axles)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the knees open, breathe in as they come back together.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s out, short hold, about 2.2 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can open fully without rocking the trunk.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate; longer hold at the open position

cues.text: Sit with your back on the pad, knees bent about 90 degrees and together, the pads on the outside of the knees and the feet on the footrests; hold the side handles.
Breathe out and push the knees apart against the pads, the thighs turning out about the hips.
Hold the open position for a moment; keep the back on the pad and the hips on the seat.
Breathe in and let the knees come back together slowly.
Pause briefly with the knees almost together without letting the stack touch down.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the trunk forward to open
mistakes.fix: Keep the back on the pad and lighten the stack.
Take about two seconds to close.
Open as far as you comfortably can and hold briefly.

kinematics.norm: From knees together to about 30-45 degrees each side (clinical opinion)
Seated, hips and knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Each arm turns on a vertical axle under the hip, so the pad stays on the outside of the knee (clinical opinion)
The gluteus medius is the main hip abductor; side-lying hip abduction ranked among the highest gluteus medius exercises (Distefano et al. 2009)
Controlled, about 1-1.5 s out and 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Lever Seated Hip Abduction, video (movement reference)
Distefano et al. 2009, gluteal muscle activation during common therapeutic exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 39(7):532-540)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The stack load is user-chosen: start light and move smoothly.
Hip or groin pain: reduce the range or skip the exercise and ask a clinician.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hip discomfort: open only part of the way.
Set the start position so the knees are not forced together.
progressions: Longer holds at the open position.
Trunk leaning slightly forward off the pad (more gluteus maximus, clinical opinion).

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Prime mover: abducts the hip (moves the thigh out to the side).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Prime mover: abducts the hip (moves the thigh out to the side).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Upper fibres help to abduct the flexed hip.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Upper fibres help to abduct the flexed hip.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis still on the seat.

guides.label: Knee out on an arc about the hip
